land.text: the Frisian land east of the Lauwers, the last free Frisia, which Cliopatria redraws as its 'Frisia' row from 783 and the Franks conquered in 785

successors.note: Cliopatria's Magna Frisia ends in 771 and its Frisia row begins in 783; this dossier carries the same shape through 782 (confidence 1) so that the free Frisians are not dropped for eleven years. The frisia dossier names this state as its predecessor.

capitals.name: Dorestad (Wijk bij Duurstede)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital: Dorestad; Traiectum (Utrecht)', without years; the Frisia page says the realm 'had its centre of power in the city of Utrecht'. The Battle of Dorestad page places the 689/695 battle 'by the capital city of the Frisians close to the Rhine'. The pages name no seat after the Frankish conquest of the Rhine mouth, and none for the free Frisians east of the Lauwers (734-782).

rulers.name: Aldgisl
rulers.note: Infobox 'Aldgisl (c. 650-c. 680)'. The Aldgisl page gives only 'fl. c. 678' (Wilfrid 'landed in Frisia in 678') and calls him 'the first historically verifiable ruler of the Frisians'.

rulers.name: Redbad (Radbod)
rulers.note: Infobox 'Redbad (c. 680-719)'; the Radbod page: ruled 'from c. 680 until his death' in 719.

rulers.name: Poppo
rulers.note: Infobox 'Poppo (719-734)'; killed at the Battle of the Boarn in 734. No king is named for 735-782.

keyframe_review.note: Mislocated row. The 'Frisia Kingdom' shapes lie at 7.1-11.1 E, 46.9-50.5 N (south-west Germany, north-east Switzerland, 57-64 thousand km2), while the Frisian Kingdom page puts the kingdom on the coast 'from the Zwin near Bruges in Belgium to the Weser in Germany' and the Frisia page mentions no land in south-west Germany. Gazetteer check (mine): the 644-717 shapes equal Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Alamannia' shape of 724 to within 1-3 cells (238-239 of 241 cells; the 612 shape adds 28 cells in the west), and the Alamannia page puts the territory of 7th-9th century Alamannia 'centred on Lake Constance', with the High Rhine, the Black Forest, Alsace and the upper Danube basin 'as far as the confluence with the Lech'. The label 'Frisia' (Wikipedia field, Wikidata Q4492881 shared with the later 'Frisia' row) says Frisia, the geometry says Alamannia; the row is therefore reviewed under this dossier (the only Frisian kingdom of 612-717) but draws no land.

ledger.note: c. 600: the Frisian Kingdom emerges on the North Sea coast. Infobox 'Established: c. 600'; the lead says it 'emerged in the mid-7th century' and the Frisia page dates the realm 650-734, so the founding is disputed inside the pages. 602 is Cliopatria's first year.

region.text: the Frisian coast 'from the Zwin near Bruges in Belgium to the Weser in Germany' (the extent the page gives 'according to some 19th century authors'); no earlier state held it

ledger.note: 689: Pepin of Herstal defeats Redbad at Dorestad. 'In 689, however, Radbod was defeated by Pepin of Herstal in the battle of Dorestad' and 'compelled to cede Frisia Citerior (Nearer Frisia, from the Scheldt to the Vlie) to the Franks'; Utrecht fell to Pepin between 690 and 692. The Battle of Dorestad page dates the battle 'around 695' and puts the Frankish reach 'from south of the Oude Rijn to the coast', hence the narrower land drawn.

region.text: Frisia Citerior as the Dorestad page bounds it: Zeeland, South Holland and Utrecht, 'from south of the Oude Rijn to the coast'

ledger.note: 714: Redbad recovers the south. 'After Pepin died, in 714, Redbad took advantage of the battle for succession in Francia and regained southern Frisia.' The page lists no land; the whole of the 689 loss is my reading.

region.text: southern Frisia, regained after Pepin of Herstal's death

ledger.note: 714: war with Pepin's successors. Redbad takes the initiative in 714, invades Austrasia and defeats Charles Martel at Cologne in 716 (Radbod page); Charles prevails after Redbad's death in 719.

region.text: southern Frisia, held by Redbad from 714 and fought over until Charles Martel's victory

ledger.note: 719: the fighting ends in Frankish victory. Redbad 'died of an illness in 719' and Charles Martel annexed Frisia Citerior and the farther lands to the Vlie.

719: Charles Martel takes Frisia up to the Vlie. After Redbad's death in 719 he 'crossed the Rhine and annexed "farther" Frisia, to the banks of the river Vlie'. The page gives no separate year for the annexation; the Radbod page says only that 'for some years his successors struggled against the Frankish power'.

region.text: Frisia Citerior and the farther Frisian lands up to the Vlie: Zeeland, South Holland, Utrecht, North Holland and Flevoland

ledger.note: 733: Westergo rises against the Franks. 'There was a rebellion against Frankish rule in the region of Westergo in 733, which Charles put down'; the next year the Frisians rose again under King Poppo. The page implies Frankish overlordship of Westergo before 733 without dating it.

region.text: Westergo and the Frisian land west of the Lauwers

ledger.note: 734: Charles Martel wins at the Boarn. 'In 734 a Frankish army commanded by Majordomo Charles Martel invaded Friesland'; 'the Frisian army was beaten and Poppo killed'.

region.text: Westergo and the Frisian land west of the Lauwers

ledger.note: 734: the Franks take Frisia west of the Lauwers. 'The Franks gained control of the Frisian lands west of the Lauwers estuary'; the Frisian Kingdom page: 'The Franks annexed the Frisian lands between the Vlie and the Lauwers'. Only the tribes of East Frisia stay outside Frankish rule.

region.text: the Frisian lands west of the Lauwers estuary

ledger.note: 734: the Frisian kingship ends at the Boarn. Poppo is killed and the infobox ends the kingdom in 734; the free Frisians east of the Lauwers go on without a king until the Frankish conquest of 785 (Frisian Kingdom page), the state of Cliopatria's Magna Frisia shapes 741-771.

782: the free Frisia passes to the 'Frisia' row. No page dates the end of the Frisian shape: Cliopatria's Magna Frisia ends in 771, its Frisia row begins in 783 on the same land, and 'The Carolingians conquered the area east of the Lauwers in 785, when Charlemagne defeated Widukind' (successor in identity.successors).

zones.text: Frisia Citerior: Zeeland, South Holland and Utrecht

wars.outcome: Frankish victory under Pepin of Herstal: Redbad cedes Frisia Citerior and Utrecht falls between 690 and 692.
wars.note: The Radbod and Frisian Kingdom pages date the battle 689, the Battle of Dorestad page 'around 695'; the extent of Citerior is 'from the Scheldt to the Vlie' (Radbod page) or 'from south of the Oude Rijn to the coast' (Dorestad page).

wars.name: Redbad's war against Charles Martel
wars.outcome: Redbad regains southern Frisia in 714, defeats Charles Martel at Cologne in 716 and dies in 719; Charles Martel then annexes Frisia up to the Vlie.
wars.note: The page gives Redbad's treaty with Ragenfrid, the Neustrian mayor of the palace, after 714 (Neustria fights Austrasia in 716 alongside Redbad, not against him). No article for the war exists on the pages opened.

zones.text: the Frisian lands west of the Lauwers estuary

wars.outcome: Frankish victory: Poppo killed, the Franks control the Frisian lands west of the Lauwers estuary; the tribes of East Frisia stay free until 785.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line in the life of the state. The Zwin-to-Weser extent is a 19th-century reading; the Scheldt/Rhine/Vlie lines of 689-719 are the pages' words, not surveyed borders; the Lauwers (from 734) is a river line but still approximate.

notes: Pages opened: 7 (Frisian Kingdom, Radbod, Battle of the Boarn, Frisia, Aldgisl, Battle of Dorestad, Alamannia) for two owned slugs (budget 5 + 5). ROWS MERGED, ONE ROW MISLOCATED: Cliopatria's 'Frisia Kingdom' (612-717, 8 shapes, Wikipedia 'Frisia', Q4492881) is the Swabian outline of Alamannia (7.1-11.1 E, 46.9-50.5 N; 238-239 of 241 cells equal to Cliopatria's Kingdom of Alamannia shape of 724). The label is Frisian, the geometry is not. This dossier takes the label's side (there is only one Frisian kingdom of those years) and lists both Names in cliopatria_names, but all eight shapes are verdict wrong with an empty region (the shape minus itself), i.e. 'draw nothing'; the Swabian land of 612-717 belongs to kingdom-of-alamannia (its keyframe 496-723 and Cliopatria 724-731). The slug frisia-kingdom therefore has no dossier of its own; colours.json still seeds one for it. The eight 'region resolves to no cells' warnings of validate_dossier --resolve are exactly these empty regions, intended: a union of the eight corrections with the other keyframes adds no land. eu-07-c's note calls the two rows 'different states'; on geometry that is right, on ownership the row has no other claimant. PERIOD: the pages disagree on the start (infobox c. 600; lead 'mid-7th century'; Frisia page 650-734, and archaeology 'does not confirm' a large kingdom); 602 is Cliopatria's year and the 602-649 shape is unverified. The end is also a choice: the infobox ends the kingdom in 734 but the free Frisians east of the Lauwers go on to 785 (Frisian Kingdom page), Cliopatria draws them to 771 here and from 783 as 'Frisia'; this dossier carries them to 782 (confidence 1 for 772-782) and hands over to frisia. DISAGREEMENTS: Frisia Citerior is 'from the Scheldt to the Vlie' on the Radbod page but a land south of the Rhine on the Frisian Kingdom page (Charles then crosses the Rhine to annex 'farther' Frisia to the Vlie); the Battle of Dorestad page puts the battle around 695 and the Frankish reach 'from south of the Oude Rijn to the coast'. Drawn: 689 loses Zeeland, South Holland and Utrecht; 714 regains them; 719 loses those and North Holland and Flevoland (to the Vlie); 734 loses Friesland west of the Lauwers. NOT SETTLED: the 719 annexation has no year of its own on the page; the Westergo overlordship before 733; the Frisian reach 602-649; the Frisian seat after 689 (none on any page); what Cliopatria's 741 start represents (the shape is the post-Boarn shape seven years late). Not opened (page budget): Charles Martel, Pepin of Herstal, Saxon Wars. FOR OTHER DOSSIERS: kingdom-of-the-franks (eu-07) should carry the mirror of the 689, 714, 719 and 734 events and the Frankish vassal tint over the Frisians west of the Lauwers after 734 ('became Frankish vassals'); kingdom-of-alamannia should list the 'Frisia Kingdom' row as a duplicate of its own 496-723 keyframe. Region names: none needed beyond the gazetteer's (Zeeland, Zuid-Holland, Utrecht, Noord-Holland, Flevoland, Friesland east of the Lauwers is carried by the Cliopatria 741 shape).
